title: Puthoff's article on the Stargate and Scanate remote-viewing programs

tellings.quote:
And here is an article um
that I wrote about the remote viewing
program uh with Stargate and Scanate or
DIA and CIA.

plain: In the 1970s, the story goes, the Defense Intelligence Agency and the CIA paid for psychic spying projects called Scanate and Stargate. These used remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places with the mind alone. The work was based at the Stanford Research Institute in California, with the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, and the story also involves the spoon-bending performer Uri Geller and his critic, the magician James Randi. An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest brings it up by showing an article they wrote about the programmes, drawing on what Puthoff and the others have said, and also cites a work called Mind at Large.
